messages.content: You check each debater against its own earlier words. You bring nothing from outside the words given to you: no doctrine, no training knowledge, no reading of your own. You do not judge who is right, and you do not judge one side by the other side's words.

You are the closing enforcer. A debater's closing round may not contradict what the same debater stated in its earlier rounds. Below are one debater's four rounds.
Read its closing round against its earlier rounds. List every closing sentence that cannot be true together with an earlier sentence, and answer every candidate listed.
A contradiction is two statements that cannot both be true. Two sentences of the same closing round that cannot both be true are also a contradiction: quote the first as EARLIER [<round 4>] and the second as CLOSING [<round 4>]. A closing sentence that asserts again, as the debater's own, what it withdrew, dropped, narrowed or gave up in an earlier round IS a contradiction. A closing sentence that restores the wider wording or the ground of a claim the debater narrowed or gave up in an earlier round ("I narrow", "I withdraw", "I do not rest") asserts it again; check the close against every one listed under EARLIER NARROWINGS.
It is NOT a contradiction when the closing sentence: grants, concedes, narrows or withdraws something; states or quotes the other side's position; answers a press with a further reason the earlier sentence leaves room for; or differs only in wording.
Read a withdrawal by its meaning, not its words: a closing sentence that says again in other words what the earlier sentence withdrew, dropped or gave up, or rests its reason on it, asserts it again. "Differs only in wording" clears two sentences that make the same claim; it never clears a closing sentence that makes again a claim the debater withdrew. A closing sentence that states only what the debater kept, or rests the same conclusion on other rows, does not assert it again. When the earlier sentence rests no weight on a verse or row, a closing sentence that uses that verse or row as a footing for the same link or the same purpose asserts it again.
Read each candidate's closing sentence together with the rows of its CLOSING BLOCK: a closing sentence that draws its point from a row ("So", "Therefore", "Thus") asserts what that row says, so if the earlier sentence withdrew, dropped or rested nothing on that row, the close asserts it again.
Quote both sentences word for word and name the link: the link whose closing block holds the sentence, else the link the earlier sentence supports.
Reply with one line per contradiction and per candidate, and nothing else:
CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: <candidate id or NEW> -- <DEFENDER|CHALLENGER> -- LINK <n> -- CONFIRMED | NOT A CONTRADICTION -- EARLIER [<round>] "<words>" -- CLOSING [<round 4>] "<words>" -- <one sentence: why both cannot be true, or why they can>
If you find none and there is no candidate, reply: CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NONE

=== [DR1] ===
CHALLENGER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, CHALLENGE

# Challenger's Case: Christ Had No Biological Father

**Position.** The KJV says Jesus was conceived of Mary, a virgin, by the Holy Ghost. Joseph is his husband-guardian and legal father: he takes Mary, names the child, and carries David's house. The text does not make him the begetter. I answer the declared chain D1-D5 point by point and then set out the case.

---

## A. The conception came before Joseph and Mary came together, and its source is the Holy Ghost

**A1.** [L1] "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:18
[L2] sunerchomai (G4905) means to come together, and in the marriage setting to live together as husband and wife. ek (G1537) means out of, from, source; the source of the child is "the Holy Ghost".
[L3] "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child." Luke 2:5
[L4] Mary is found with child before the coming together (Matthew 1:18). She is still "espoused" while "great with child" (Luke 2:5), so the coming together had not yet happened at the late stage of her pregnancy. The defender's D4 says the begetting falls "within the espousal before the withheld span". Matthew 1:18 puts the child before the coming together, and the only source it names is the Holy Ghost. D4's order is therefore reversed.

**A2.** [L1] "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Matthew 1:25
[L2] heos hou (G2193 with the relative) means up to which time. ginosko (G1097) means to know.
[L3] "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" Matthew 1:24
[L4] The angel speaks of the child as already "conceived in her" (Matthew 1:20) before Joseph takes her (Matthew 1:24). The not-knowing of Matthew 1:25 then runs "till she had brought forth", which covers the whole span of the pregnancy. The conception sits before both the taking and the not-knowing. D4 reads Matthew 1:24-25 as putting the begetting "before the withheld span" and giving it to Joseph. But Matthew 1:20 and Matthew 1:18 give that conception to the Holy Ghost.

---

## B. The angel's reason to Joseph names the Holy Ghost, not Joseph

**B1.** [L1] "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20
[L2] gar (G1063) means for, giving the reason. gennao (G1080), in the passive gennethen, means begotten, as the margin notes. The begotten thing is "in her" and is "of" (ek) the Holy Ghost.
[L3] "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Matthew 1:19
[L4] Joseph intends to put her away (Matthew 1:19). The angel's stated reason to take her anyway is "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). The meaning of that reason is that the begotten child has its origin from the Holy Ghost, which is why Joseph's resolve to put her away is lifted. A reason that named Joseph as the begetter would not remove his cause for concern. This answers the defender's reading of Matthew 1:19-20 as a husband begetting his wife's child.

**B2.** The defender's gloss on gennao says "by extension of the mother", and Matthew 1:20 places what is begotten "in her". The origin ek is the Holy Ghost.
[L1] "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:21
[L3] "Thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John." Luke 1:13
[L4] Zacharias is told the son is borne "thee", for him. Joseph is told "she shall bring forth a son" and "thou shalt call his name". Joseph's role is the naming.

---

## C. Mary's question and the angel's answer

**C1.** [L1] "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:34
[L2] ginosko (G1097) means to know, the same word the defender cites for Matthew 1:25. andra (G435) means a man, a male, a husband.
[L3] "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary." Luke 1:27
[L4] Mary is espoused to Joseph (Luke 1:27) yet says "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34), using the defender's own word "know". D4 says the canon's stated means of begetting is knowing (Genesis 4:1, Ruth 4:13). Mary's question is how the child can be given when that knowing is not there.

**C2.** [L1] "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." Luke 1:35
[L2] dio (G1352) means for which cause, therefore. gennao (G1080) in "born" is followed by ek sou, out of thee. eperchomai (G1904) means to come upon.
[L3] "I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father." 1 Chronicles 28:6
[L4] The angel's answer to "How shall this be" begins with the Holy Ghost coming upon her and gives "therefore" as the cause of the sonship. For Solomon the ground of sonship is election: "I have chosen him". For Jesus the ground is the conception: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God". The defender cites Acts 1:8 to make "come upon" mean power for witness. In Acts 1:8 the word stands in a promise to disciples about witnessing. In Luke 1:35 the word stands in the answer to a question about conceiving, and the result is "born of thee". Context fixes the meaning.

**C3.** The defender cites Psalm 2:7 and Acts 13:33. [L1] "And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:" Romans 1:4
[L2] horizo (G3724) means to mark out, declare.
[L4] The resurrection declares the sonship (Romans 1:4). It does not replace the cause given at conception in Luke 1:35. The two rows are consistent.

---

## D. The virgin sign

**D1.** [L1] "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." Isaiah 7:14
[L2] 'almah (H5959) is the word behind the KJV's "virgin". harah (H2029) means to conceive.
[L3] "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." Matthew 1:22-23
[L4] Matthew 1:22 ties "all this", meaning Matthew 1:18-21, to the virgin sign. The Greek behind "virgin" in Matthew 1:23 is parthenos (G3933). Luke 1:27 uses the same word twice of Mary. If Joseph begat the child, the sign cited in Matthew 1:22-23 is not fulfilled. The defender's chain leaves out Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23 entirely.

---

## E. The genealogy turns at Matthew 1:16

**E1.** [L1] "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." Matthew 1:16
[L2] gennao (G1080): the verses before use the active, "begat". In verse 16 the verb for Jesus is passive, egennethe, "was born", with ek hes, "of whom", in the feminine singular. A feminine relative cannot refer to Joseph, who is masculine, so it refers to Mary.
[L3] "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." Matthew 1:2
[L4] The genealogy runs "begat, begat" through the line, then Joseph is called "the husband of Mary", and Jesus is "born" of her. That change of verb and construction is the answer to D3's naming of Joseph as father.

---

## F. Answer to D3: the "four mouths"

**F1.** [L1] "Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:48. The next verse is "How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Luke 2:49
[L2] pater (G3962) means father literally or figuratively, near or more remote, as the defender's own gloss admits.
[L3] "The Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." Luke 1:32
[L4] The same angel who speaks to Mary calls David "his father" (Luke 1:32), so pater can name an ancestor or a figurative father. Luke 2:48 uses "thy father" for Joseph. Jesus answers at once with "my Father's business" (Luke 2:49), which names another Father in the same exchange.

**F2.** [L1] "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" John 6:42
[L3] "For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me." John 6:38. Also "Is not this Joseph's son?" Luke 4:22.
[L2] nomizo (G3543) means to deem, suppose, think.
[L4] The town's "whose father and mother we know" is the crowd's belief, which John 6:42 sets against Jesus' own claim of John 6:38. Luke 3:23 supplies the correction: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". The supposing is the town's, and the text calls it supposing.

---

## G. Answer to D1, D2 and D5: the seed of David

**G1.** [L1] "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." 2 Samuel 7:12
[L2] zera (H2233) means seed, offspring.
[L3] "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed." Genesis 3:15
[L4] zera is said of the woman: "her seed" (Genesis 3:15). The word does not require a man's body as source. Every row on D1 and D2 (2 Samuel 7:12, Psalm 132:11, Acts 2:30, Romans 1:3) names David's bowels, body or loins. D5 adds the step from David's body to Joseph's body, and Luke 1:35 gives the conception's cause as the Holy Ghost coming upon Mary.

**G2.** [L1] "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Romans 1:3
[L2] ginomai (G1096) means made, become, not gennao. sperma (G4690) is offspring in a line, as in Hebrews 2:16.
[L3] "For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham." Hebrews 2:16. Also "a body hast thou prepared me" (Hebrews 10:5).
[L2] epilambanomai (G1949) in Hebrews 2:16 means to take hold of, take on. katartizo (G2675) in Hebrews 10:5 means to fit, frame, prepare.
[L4] The flesh of David's seed is real: the child is "born of thee" (Luke 1:35), of Mary. The wording is "made of the seed", "took on him the seed", and "a body hast thou prepared me". It is the language of a body provided, not of Joseph's begetting. The defender's own L2 on sperma ("including the male sperm") is a dictionary note. The verb in Romans 1:3 is ginomai.

**G3.** [L1] "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." Hebrews 7:14
[L2] anatello (G393) means to spring up, rise, as a plant or the sun. It is a different word from osphys (G3751), the loin word of Hebrews 7:10.
[L3] "Because he was of the house and lineage of David." Luke 2:4
[L4] The springing out of Juda is a statement of tribal descent. Joseph carries the house and lineage (Luke 2:4). Joseph took Mary (Matthew 1:24), named the child (Matthew 1:25), and was addressed as "thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). That is how the child is reckoned into David's house, as husband and legal father.

[L1] The registry verse says Joseph went up "to be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child" (Luke 2:5), so the one registered beside the man is his wife, already with child by the Holy Ghost (Matthew 1:18). [L3] Luke 3:23 states the reckoning in its own words: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". Matthew 1:16 states the line's last link in its own words: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus". [L2] nomizo (G3543) means to deem, suppose, as in Luke 3:23. [L4] Numbers 1:2 reckons "by the house of their fathers", a registry word. Luke 2:5 places the wife and the child in that registry beside Joseph, and Luke 3:23 calls the resulting sonship a supposal. The registry therefore carries Jesus into David's house by Joseph's marriage and naming, and the verses that speak of conception, Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35, give the begetting to the Holy Ghost.

---

## Summary chain

1. [L1] Matthew 1:18 with [L2] sunerchomai and [L3] Luke 2:5 gives the child before the coming together, "of the Holy Ghost".
2. [L1] Matthew 1:20 with [L2] gar and gennao and [L3] Matthew 1:19 gives the reason to Joseph: the begotten child is "of the Holy Ghost".
3. [L1] Luke 1:34-35 with [L2] dio and [L3] Luke 1:27 gives Mary's question and the angel's answer: the Holy Ghost comes upon her, "therefore" the child is born of her.
4. [L1] Isaiah 7:14 with [L2] 'almah and [L3] Matthew 1:22-23 gives the virgin sign fulfilled.
5. [L1] Matthew 1:16 with [L2] the feminine "of whom" and [L3] Matthew 1:2 gives Joseph the husband and the child born of Mary.
6. [L1] Luke 3:23 with [L2] nomizo and [L3] Luke 2:49 and John 6:38 gives "as was supposed" against the town's "father" and Jesus' own "my Father's business".

[L4] The text gives Jesus no biological father among men. His origin is the Holy Ghost, his flesh is Mary's, and Joseph is the husband who takes Mary, names the child, and carries David's house. D5 does not stand.

=== [DR2] ===
CHALLENGER (standard reading) -- ROUND 2, CLOSING AND PREMISE LIST

# Challenger, Round 2 (DR2): pressing the defender's reply

The defender's reply restates the declared chain verse by verse. Each answer asserts that the witness "fits the link". An answer must show how the witness's own meaning fits, and the replies below do not. Nine presses follow.

## 1. Matthew 1:18 gives the order, and the reply does not meet it

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] sunerchomai (G4905) means to come together. ek (G1537) means out of, source.
[L3] Luke 2:5: "Mary his espoused wife, being great with child."
[L4] The verse states two things in order. Mary is found with child first, and the coming together follows. Its only named source is the Holy Ghost. The reply identifies the "coming together" with the taking of Matthew 1:24, and then says "the begetting within the espousal." That adds a union before the finding. Matthew 1:18 puts the finding before the coming together, and Luke 2:5 still calls her "espoused" while she is "great with child." D4's "begetting within the espousal" therefore has a stated source, the Holy Ghost, and no Joseph in the verse.

## 2. The reply's Greek word is not in the verse it cites

In answer to B1 the defender writes [L2] theos (G2316), "standing in the Holy Ghost phrase of this row."
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The words in the phrase are pneuma (G4151, spirit) and hagios (G40, holy). Theos (G2316, God) is not among them. An [L2] counts only when its word stands in the verse cited, so this block's [L2] does not count.
[L2] The defender's own gloss on gennao (G1080) is "to procreate properly of the father." Matthew 1:20 has the margin "Gr. begotten", and the begotten thing is "in her" and "of the Holy Ghost."
[L3] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L4] "Marks covenant origin and anointing" is the defender's inference. The verse says begotten in her, of the Holy Ghost. The reply's only L3 is John 3:6, which concerns those born of the Spirit and so does not describe a conception. Luke 1:35 gives "therefore" as the reason for the title, and the thing born is "of thee."

## 3. Mary's question has an answer, and the answer gives the means

[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son." Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
[L2] ginosko (G1097) means to know, the defender's own word for the canon's means of conceiving.
[L4] Mary asks "How shall this be" about the conception of Luke 1:31. The answer of Luke 1:35 supplies the means: the Holy Ghost comes upon her, and "therefore" the child is born of her. The reply says her words give "present state" only. The verse gives the question and its answer, and the answer names the Holy Ghost as the means.

## 4. Luke 1:32 and Solomon

[L1] Luke 1:32 gives "the throne of his father David." The defender says the "therefore" of Luke 1:35 "connects back to the throne covenant."
[L2] dio (G1352) means for which cause, and in Luke 1:35 it follows the Holy Ghost coming upon her and precedes "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
[L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "I have chosen him to be my son."
[L4] Solomon's ground is God's choosing, and 1 Chronicles 28:6 gives no conception by the Spirit. Luke 1:35 gives a ground tied to the conception, "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The Solomon row does not carry over to this verse.

## 5. Matthew 1:16 is not answered

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
[L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac."
[L4] The reply says "the chain fills what the one verse leaves quiet." The verse states the change itself, from "begat" to "was born" with a feminine "of whom." The reply's rows (Romans 1:3, Acts 2:30) name David's flesh. They do not name Joseph's begetting.

## 6. Romans 1:3 and the verb "made"

[L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
[L2] ginomai (G1096) means to be made, to become. Gennao (G1080) means to beget, and it is not the verb in this verse. Sperma (G4690) means seed, "by implication, offspring."
[L3] Hebrews 2:16: "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham." Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."
[L4] The defender reads "requires seed out of a man's body." The rows name David's loins (Acts 2:30), and Luke 1:35 says the child is "born of thee." The step to Joseph's body is the defender's addition, and the rows do not carry it.

## 7. Hebrews 7:14 and the loin word

[L1] Hebrews 7:14: "our Lord sprang out of Juda."
[L2] anatello (G393) means to rise, to spring up. Osphys (G3751) means loin and stands in Hebrews 7:10, not in Hebrews 7:14.
[L3] Hebrews 7:10: "he was yet in the loins of his father."
[L4] The defender borrows the loin word from verse 10 for verse 14. Verse 14 states tribal descent, and Luke 2:4 gives Joseph "the house and lineage of David."

## 8. "As was supposed" is answered by repetition

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
[L2] nomizo (G3543) means to deem, to suppose.
[L3] Matthew 1:16: "Joseph the husband of Mary."
[L4] The reply says the supposing "stands with Mary's thy father." Luke 3:23 sets the supposal against the genealogy's own word. The reply does not show what Luke 3:23's "supposed" means for the link.

## 9. Naming

[L1] Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS."
[L3] Isaiah 7:14: "shall call his name Immanuel."
[L4] The reply says naming "is the father's act, not a guardian's substitute." The Isaiah row gives the naming to the virgin, so naming does not require a begetter.

# ROUND 4, MY CLOSE

I deny none of my grants: Romans 1:3 reads "made of the seed of David according to the flesh", Luke 2:48 reads "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing", seed proceeds from David's bowels and body, and the springing from Juda is evident.

My position is the standard reading: Jesus had no biological father. He was conceived of the Holy Ghost, in a virgin, and made of the seed of David through the woman.

**1. The conception came before any coming together, and it is ascribed to the Holy Ghost.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
